data.raw_text:
I remember about a year ago, I think it was when Nano Banana first came out, the data training was sooo good when it comes to certain regional nuances. I generated a lot of images, some using real locations of the place where I live, as well as other Southeast Asian countries that I've visited countless times for work.

Then I remember there's this one anon account. Not really sure who they were, because they had no profile pic, but on their bio they wrote something about being a filmmaker, industry expert for more than 20 years and so on. I couldn't confirm where they're based because back then on X, you couldn't see someone's location like you can now.

And yeah, as typical with most AI haters, they attacked me. Being told that my work is AI slop and so on is quite... well, an everyday thing I guess. Not something surprising anymore. 😆😆

But what's interesting is that this person also used the opportunity to attack me with racial slurs and quite insane I guess LOL. 

Basically, that account said something like my AI slop is as trashy as the third world place that I'm living in, saying only Singapore is the only first world country in Southeast Asia.

I wasn't angry. I was more like... whoa. Who hurt you? It felt like this person was channeling all their hatred into a single comment, from AI slop all the way to life in Southeast Asia.

I smiled. And I really did smile. Because the "trashy region" they mentioned is actually my most favorite place in the world. I'm assuming that person came from the western side of the world, and just like with China, somehow Southeast Asia has been presented in such a wrong way, especially by Western legacy media.

But that insult actually inspired me so much. It became the main fuel. Like yeah, I wanna show the vibe of this region I love so much.

And let me give you a bit of context. 

I spent most of my entire childhood and teen years overseas since my late father was a diplomat. And yeah, as diplomats we moved a lot. I used to live in San Francisco, Geneva, Tokyo, Singapore, Australia, Turkey. So I haven't really been living in my own country during my childhood.

It was after I graduated from a university in Sydney, Australia, and was ready to start a career, that I finally settled longer in Indonesia. I told my dad, give me one year to catch up with everything in my own country, then after that I'll start working. So for that time I stayed with my uncle in Yogyakarta.

And holy shiiiit.

This was the first time I actually experienced real culture shock. I guess for my entire life I'd been living in places that are quite systematic and organized. Then here I am in Yogyakarta, and my point of view was very similar to any foreigner living in Southeast Asia for the first time.

During my early time in Yogyakarta... I was like... damnnnnn... this place is sooooo chill. And the people here are sooooo nice. Like seriously, genuinely nice. And it becomes even more surreal knowing these are actually my own people.

It's amazing how you can just sit down with a random person at a warung stall, smoking, enjoying a coffee, having a very fun and casual conversation for almost 4 hours, and then you'll never see that person again for the rest of your life. You don't even know their names.

And yeah, next day it happens again. You encounter new people, you talk about sports, current issues, women (lol, we love our women so much), and then yeah, you never see them again either. But it was that experience, the warmth and friendliness of the people there, that really made me happy and left such a lasting impression. And it was also the same things before I went to Bali.

Then I moved to Jakarta, the main capital. It's sooo damn chaotic, brutal, traffic everywhere, you name it. But always, always, no matter how chaotic the city is, once you sit down with people and engage in a conversation, it feels like you're seeing the real true warmness of the people. They might be tired from the daily hustle, but once you sit down together, drink some tea or coffee, we call that "Nongkrong", it's sooo much fun.

From there I started working at an ad agency that gave me the opportunity to travel frequently across Southeast Asia. Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, the Philippines, Vietnam. 

It was also during this time that I worked a lot with Thai creative directors. They are insanely talented, which is why the Thai ads industry still remains my top inspiration. All of this gave me even more love for this region. So it makes sense that we call each other SEAblings.

Whenever I visit these countries, despite the languages being different, somehow our body language is the same. The feeling doesn't feel foreign. And this region has become the place where I built my life.

The region in which that account called "trash third world" is an absolute paradise for me.

Ever since then, it became my drive, my inspiration behind every AI content that I make. I literally wanna show it as it is. Not through some filtered western lens. Not through someone's idea of what "third world" looks like. Just as it is.

A place filled with very nice people and a vibe that you honestly can't find anywhere else. A place where strangers become friends over a cup of coffee at a warung, where chaos and warmth live side by side, where the hustle is real but so is the heart.

It was also here where I met my wife. A Sundanese-Chinese girl. We used to work at the same company, but eventually she had to resign and move back to Bandung. And at that moment, I told myself, there's nooooo way I will let this woman vanish like any other stranger in my life. I really wanted to be with her. So every weekend, I made the trip to Bandung just to see her. Back then, going to Bandung wasn't like it is now. It was insane, could take 3.5 hours, sometimes even 5 hours. 

And back then there was no WhatsApp, we only had SMS hahaha. No social media like today. So when you finally see her, damnnnnn the longing was just so intense. And the moment you finally meet, it's not even like a big dramatic hug or anything. You just stand there, looking at each other, almost tearing up because damn... you just miss this woman so much. But I just wanted to see her. We'd meet up, I'd take her out for some mie ayam, nothing fancy, but my heart was already so full and happy. And eventually we got married, and now I'm blessed with 3 kids, all boys hahahaha. And she still wants a 4th one, but I think we're good.

All of that, i want to express it with my Ai work.
And if my work can capture even a small piece of that, then that anonymous hater did me the biggest favor. Because they reminded me exactly why I do this.

And honestly? I hope that person finds their peace too. I hold no grudge, because eventually we are just strangers here. Whatever frustration made them lash out like that, it will never change any single thing about their life or mine.

This region is home. It raised me, shaped me, and gave me every reason to keep creating

data.raw_text:
#news #geopolitics #LamatinaleduBourdillon aka #CanardHirsute (Shaggy Duck)
-----------------

Hello everyone, I hope you’re all well. The sun is shining and the day is sure to be a lovely one for you and your loved ones, full of positive emotional experiences (hello Twitter Algorithm, which, it seems, has become a bit of a sourpuss in this regard since the start of the year, with a corresponding drop in audience figures). According to well-informed sources contacted by Shaggy Duck, gangs of blue teddy bears are running all over the world chasing pink rabbits to give them kisses.
Meanwhile, as for war, conflicts and crises, it’s business as usual;
-------------------------------------
1 Iran
Oil prices soared again on Monday, rising 8% to $91 a barrel, following renewed tensions between Washington and Tehran. Iran vowed on Monday to “retaliate soon” against the US Navy’s seizure of one of its cargo ships, with the Iranian military spokesman describing the seizure as an “act of armed piracy”. Donald Trump had announced earlier that the US Navy had opened fire on the Iranian cargo ship Touska in the Gulf of Oman and had taken control of it. The ship “attempted to breach our naval blockade, and it was a mistake,” the US president wrote on his Truth Social platform. Iran does not currently intend to engage in talks with the United States, Iranian state television reported on Sunday evening. Finally, a vessel belonging to the French shipping company CMA CGM “was fired upon with warning shots yesterday” in the Strait of Hormuz, the French shipping group said on Sunday, adding that the crew was “safe and sound”.
And Donald Trump announced that a US delegation would be in Pakistan on Monday to restart negotiations with Iran, whilst threatening to destroy “all power stations and all bridges in Iran” should the talks fail – which, according to Canard Hirsute, would be utter nonsense, but dogs that bark don’t always bite. Vice-President JD Vance, who had already led the delegation to Islamabad on 11 April for talks at an unprecedented level but which ended in failure, will once again be accompanied by Mr Trump’s two usual emissaries, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. Apparently, they will simply be sightseeing in Islamabad, a city not exactly known for its seaside charm.
-----------------------
2 Robots
On Sunday in Beijing, humanoid robots broke the human world record for the half-marathon for the first time, illustrating China’s spectacular technological advances in the sector. The Yizhuang Half-Marathon saw robots, standing on two legs, compete against humans.
The champion robot, equipped with an autonomous navigation system and representing the Chinese smartphone brand Honor, completed the 21 kilometres in 50 minutes. This is significantly faster than the men’s world record (57 minutes 20 seconds), held by the Ugandan Jacob Kiplimo. In the 2025 edition, the winning robot had taken three times as long, which is the time Canard Hirsute would have achieved. The machines’ movements were much smoother this year and the number of participating teams rose from around twenty to a hundred.
-----------------
3 Spain
Pedro Sánchez, Prime Minister of a dual aircraft carrier of China and Islamism in Europe, currently better known as ‘Spain’ (though, well, that should change at the next election), announced on Sunday evening 19 agreements with Beijing, which he supports as a mediator in the Middle East. On his fourth visit to China in three years, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez expressed his support for greater Chinese involvement in the world order. On Tuesday, he will also call on the European Union to terminate its association agreement with Israel, arguing that its government “violates international law”. “We will not accept a hypocritical interpretation from someone who forges ties with totalitarian regimes that violate human rights, such as Erdogan’s Turkey or Nicolas Maduro’s Venezuela,” retorted Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar.
------------------------
4 Bulgaria
Former President Rumen Radev’s Democratic Bulgaria coalition came out well ahead in Sunday’s general election with 38% of the vote, according to exit polls. The conservatives (GERB) led by former Prime Minister Boyko Borisov, who headed the previous government, came second with 16% of the vote, followed by the liberals of the PP-DB (14%). This result reshuffles the deck for forming a government in this Balkan country, which has voted for the eighth time in five years, although Mr Radev, 62, has not yet named a partner to form a coalition. Rumen Radev, who is generally pro-Kremlin and must now secure a majority in the 240-seat Parliament, had ruled out a coalition with Boyko Borisov before the elections, citing their “disagreement over corruption”.
-------------------
5 France
Members of LR gave a boost on Sunday to party leader Bruno Retailleau’s bid for the Élysée by propelling him directly into the race without going through the primary process. A reflex of blind support for the leader in keeping with the Bonapartist culture of this party, which is now but a shadow of the one that dominated French political life from 1944 until recently.
This resounding victory, with 73.8% of the vote, certainly lends legitimacy to the LR leader, who launched his presidential bid in February ahead of the vote. But the 60% turnout, with nearly 45,000 voters, does not necessarily nip in the bud the idea of an open primary in the autumn to select a single candidate for the right and centre. This result was expected: the contest was all but decided, as no rival had expressed a wish to cross swords with the former Minister of the Interior. Heading towards 4.7% (and perhaps the party’s collapse). This vote makes it difficult to organise a primary for the right and centre in the autumn, as many barons of Les Républicains (LR), former LR members or others are calling for, as it would force Retailleau to disavow the activists’ vote.
---------------------
6 China
China has dispatched a group of warships to conduct exercises in the western Pacific Ocean, a move that comes as Japan takes part for the first time in large-scale manoeuvres with the United States and the Philippines, highlighting the growing tensions between Tokyo and Beijing. The Chinese navy has deployed a naval task force led by the Type 052D destroyer Baotou to transit between the Japanese islands of Amami Oshima and Yokoate. These Chinese exercises also come just days after China criticised Tokyo for sending a warship into the Taiwan Strait.

This is significantly faster than the men’s world record (57 minutes 20 seconds), held by the Ugandan Jacob Kiplimo. In the 2025 edition, the winning robot had taken three times as long, which is the time Canard Hirsute would have achieved. The machines’ movements were much smoother this year and the number of participating teams rose from around twenty to a hundred. ----------------- 3 Spain Pedro Sánchez, Prime Minister of a dual aircraft carrier of China and Islamism in Europe, currently better known as ‘Spain’ (though, well, that should change at the next election), announced on Sunday evening 19 agreements with Beijing, which he supports as a mediator in the Middle East. On his fourth visit to China in three years, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez expressed his support for greater Chinese involvement in the world order. On Tuesday, he will also call on the European Union to terminate its association agreement with Israel, arguing that its government “violates international law”. “We will not accept a hypocritical interpretation from someone who forges ties with totalitarian regimes that violate human rights, such as Erdogan’s Turkey or Nicolas Maduro’s Venezuela,” retorted Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar. ------------------------ 4 Bulgaria Former President Rumen Radev’s Democratic Bulgaria coalition came out well ahead in Sunday’s general election with 38% of the vote, according to exit polls. The conservatives (GERB) led by former Prime Minister Boyko Borisov, who headed the previous government, came second with 16% of the vote, followed by the liberals of the PP-DB (14%). This result reshuffles the deck for forming a government in this Balkan country, which has voted for the eighth time in five years, although Mr Radev, 62, has not yet named a partner to form a coalition. Rumen Radev, who is generally pro-Kremlin and must now secure a majority in the 240-seat Parliament, had ruled out a coalition with Boyko Borisov before the elections, citing their “disagreement over corruption”. ------------------- 5 France Members of LR gave a boost on Sunday to party leader Bruno Retailleau’s bid for the Élysée by propelling him directly into the race without going through the primary process. A reflex of blind support for the leader in keeping with the Bonapartist culture of this party, which is now but a shadow of the one that dominated French political life from 1944 until recently. This resounding victory, with 73.8% of the vote, certainly lends legitimacy to the LR leader, who launched his presidential bid in February ahead of the vote. But the 60% turnout, with nearly 45,000 voters, does not necessarily nip in the bud the idea of an open primary in the autumn to select a single candidate for the right and centre. This result was expected: the contest was all but decided, as no rival had expressed a wish to cross swords with the former Minister of the Interior. Heading towards 4.7% (and perhaps the party’s collapse). This vote makes it difficult to organise a primary for the right and centre in the autumn, as many barons of Les Républicains (LR), former LR members or others are calling for, as it would force Retailleau to disavow the activists’ vote. --------------------- 6 China China has dispatched a group of warships to conduct exercises in the western Pacific Ocean, a move that comes as Japan takes part for the first time in large-scale manoeuvres with the United States and the Philippines, highlighting the growing tensions between Tokyo and Beijing. The Chinese navy has deployed a naval task force led by the Type 052D destroyer Baotou to transit between the Japanese islands of Amami Oshima and Yokoate. These Chinese exercises also come just days after China criticised Tokyo for sending a warship into the Taiwan Strait.

BAGONG AIRCRAFT RESCUE AND FIRE FIGHTING UNITS

Nag-deploy ang Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines (CAAP) ng bagong units ng Aircraft Rescue and Fire Fighting (ARFF) vehicles sa mga regional airport bilang bahagi ng patuloy na modernization ng airport emergency response capabilities.

Dumating sa Laoag International Airport ang Oshkosh Striker 6x6 fire truck nitong Linggo, April 19. Kasunod ito ng naunang delivery ng isa pang unit sa Puerto Princesa International Airport noong April 18.

Nakatakda naman i-deploy ang additional ARFF units sa Butuan Airport, Siargao Airport, Busuanga Airport, Bicol International Airport, General Santos International Airport, at Tacloban Airport.

📸: CAAP

PINSALANG DULOT NG SUNOG SA NAVOTAS SANITARY LANDFILL

Ibinahagi ng Manila City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Department (MCDRRMD) ang thermal drone images na nagpapakita ng lawak ng pinsalang idinulot ng sunog sa Navotas Sanitary Landfill.

Isa ang sunog sa mga sinasabing dahilan ng paglala ng polusyon sa hangin.

Naitala ang air quality na nasa kategoryang “Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups” sa ilang bahagi ng Maynila, batay sa latest advisory ng lokal na pamahalaan ngayong Lunes, April 20.

📸: Manila PIO (Facebook)

The GoI is definitely working against corruption in all departments. I keep seeing such news where GoI's own agencies keep getting the corrupt in many of GoI organizations.

Corruption in India has become a culture, especially in state and central govt orgs. Ingrained over decades of license raj and corrupt governments. It will take years to clean up more.

But one thing patriotic Indians must be beware of is the adversaries are using corruption by local officials in democracies to incite the public against the central government these days.

This is the new communist method coming from one country to destabilize, using psyops, democracies with governments not favorable to them. Like they have tried in the Philippines, Indonesia, Argentina etc.

Be it infra woes or corruption, we can clearly see a pattern of public incitement amplifying them. A lot of people immediately say "So you don't want us to protest against the government for this or that issue?"

Not at all. But don't become a useful sepoy of the adversaries to be used to destabilize your own country, your life, cause anarchy, and push yourself into economic misery they can take advantage of.
